fit: canola oil in a mixed MS diet and Modified Fatigue Impact Scale
assessment: NICE lists canola and olive oil within the diet and gives an unadjusted difference of -0.70 MFIS points (95% CI -5.34 to 3.94). Original abstract reports a favorable p=.001. The original adjustment and precise refining grade remain unresolved. No canola-specific or Parkinson estimate.

fit: distilled cinnamon-containing mixture and rated fatigue in multiple sclerosis
assessment: Means moved 3.729 to 2.213 versus 3.520 to 5.066. Group p=.353, group-by-time p<.001. Printed SDs and intervals and the withdrawal counts conflict. Multiple ingredients and distillation prevent isolation of ground cinnamon.

fit: registered six-herb oral capsule and secondary fatigue outcomes
assessment: Registry reports 93 enrolled and completed, with FSS and daily diary fatigue measures. No numerical results posted. The linked protocol describes a shorter duration than the current registry, and neither provides a separate ground cinnamon treatment.

fit: green or white tea allowed in a mixed multiple-sclerosis diet measuring fatigue
assessment: NICE lists optional tea in the prescribed diet and an inconclusive unadjusted MFIS endpoint. The original abstract reports a favorable separate comparison. No measured intake, separately assigned brewed tea, or Parkinson fatigue estimate.

fit: isolated oral eugenol and evoked thermal or mechanical rat responses
assessment: Day-five thermal latency 11.4 versus 6.1 seconds, p<.01. Mechanical tests were inconclusive and did not generate allodynia. The formulation differed from the saline comparator. Neither arm corresponds to ground clove or clinical Parkinson pain.
